summary.title: Anatomy of a finished pack
points: A pack holds tablets, primary packaging, the leaflet, the carton and safety features.
Each part has its own supplier, specification and lead time.
Primary packaging touches the product, so it's part of the quality data.
Secondary packaging carries the legal texts and codes.
Printed items depend on approved artwork and often arrive last.

exercises.scenario: You list the components for a new launch.

questions.prompt: Which change would usually need new stability data?
options: A new font on the leaflet
A new carton board from another mill, with the same print

questions.prompt: Which items are usually last to arrive?
options: The printed ones: foil, leaflet, carton
The tablets, because manufacturing always runs last

exercises.scenario: A colleague says 'packaging is just the box'.

questions.prompt: What does the carton carry that matters for launch?
options: The stability data that justify the shelf life
The carton, because it holds the blisters
questions.explanation: It's in contact with the product's environment.

summary.title: API and excipients
points: In many tablets, the API is a small part of the weight; excipients make up the rest.
Roles: filler, binder, disintegrant, lubricant, film coat.
Each excipient comes from a qualified supplier.
Excipients with known effect, like lactose or sodium, must be declared on carton and leaflet.
A formulation change can reach artwork if such an excipient is involved.

exercises.scenario: The formulator replaces mannitol with lactose as filler.

questions.prompt: Why does the artwork team care?
options: All filler changes need a new carton colour
Lactose is an excipient with known effect, so it must be declared
Only the leaflet's font must change
questions.explanation: Carton and leaflet must declare it.

questions.prompt: Which excipient stops tablets sticking to the press?
options: Cellulose, which is used as a filler

exercises.scenario: Purchasing changes the supplier of the binder, with no change of material.

options: Nothing, since the material is identical
A new BE study and a new DCP
Not unless the excipient itself changes
Yes, always when a supplier changes
Yes, the supplier's name is on the carton
questions.explanation: Supplier names aren't on the pack.

summary.title: Primary packaging
points: It keeps out moisture, light and oxygen; the registered pack is the one stability supports.
PVC or PVC/PVDC: moderate moisture protection. Alu/Alu: high protection.
HDPE bottles often carry a desiccant and sometimes a child-resistant closure.
Materials need a specification and must meet Ph. Eur.
Changing it usually needs stability data and a variation: a project, not a purchase.

exercises.scenario: Purchasing proposes a cheaper blister film to save 3% per pack.

options: Nothing, as long as the film looks identical to the old one
It likely needs stability data and a variation first

questions.prompt: How should the change be planned?
options: As a project with owners and dates
As a Type IA notification sent after use

exercises.scenario: One market wants a bottle instead of the registered blister.

options: Stability data for the bottle and approval
Nothing, if the bottle has a desiccant
A new BE study comparing bottle and blister tablets
questions.explanation: A new pack type needs its own data.

options: Blocks light from reaching the tablets

summary.title: The carton
points: The carton carries the outer packaging particulars required by law.
Name, strength, form, active substance, excipients with known effect, pack size, storage, MAH, licence no., batch, expiry.
Plus Braille, the national Blue Box and the safety features.
Size is fixed by the packaging line; everything must fit legibly.
Printing follows artwork approval and printer lead time: order once final.

exercises.scenario: A draft carton lacks a storage condition, though the SmPC has one.

options: It's a required particular, so the artwork must be corrected
None, storage conditions are only needed in the leaflet
questions.explanation: Storage conditions are an outer particular.

questions.prompt: Which item must appear on an EU carton?
options: The batch number and expiry date

exercises.scenario: Marketing wants to add three languages to one carton.

options: A fixed carton size set by the packaging line
The QRD template forbids more than two languages
After QP release of the batch they'll be used for
Before artwork drafts, to save time
As soon as the country artwork is final
questions.explanation: Then the printer's lead time runs.

summary.title: Supplier qualification
points: Under GMP, materials come only from approved suppliers, including packaging and printed items.
Qualification: specification, risk assessment, supplier documents, audit or questionnaire.
Owned by QA with purchasing; output is an approved supplier and incoming-control rules.
Risk sets the depth; excipients need a formal GMP risk assessment.
A new supplier for a launch component must be approved before printing or delivery.

exercises.scenario: A carton printer offers a slot two weeks earlier but isn't approved.

options: A variation to the marketing authorisation for the carton printer
The QP's signature on the proof
Only a purchase order and a proof
Supplier qualification by QA, plus change control

questions.prompt: How long does qualification usually take?
options: Weeks, longer if an on-site audit is needed
About two years, like a technology transfer

exercises.scenario: QA plans a deep audit of the shipping-case supplier and a light check of the excipient supplier.

options: The depth should follow risk: the excipient deserves more
Nothing; every supplier gets the same check
Shipping cases always need on-site audits

questions.prompt: What extra is required for excipient suppliers?
options: A formal risk assessment of the appropriate GMP

summary.title: Devices and special components
points: Some products include a device: measuring cup, oral syringe, pen, inhaler.
A separate device is CE-marked on its own and included in the pack.
An integral device forms one product with the medicine (e.g. a pre-filled pen).
Integral devices need a notified-body opinion in the application.
Add the device supplier, CE marking or opinion, and lead time to the plan.

exercises.scenario: An oral solution comes with a separate measuring syringe.

options: A notified-body opinion inside the marketing authorisation application
Its own CE marking as a medical device
The syringe supplier, its CE status and lead time
questions.explanation: Device items have their own path.

exercises.scenario: A generic pre-filled pen is planned.

questions.prompt: What's different from a separate device?
options: It's approved as a medical device only
It needs no CE assessment at all
The application needs a notified-body opinion on the device part
Every pack needs a CE-marked device

summary.title: Ripple effects of a change
points: Every component ties to a specification, a supplier, the dossier and the artwork.
Ask: change control or supplier qualification? Variation, which type?
Does it affect stability? Does it touch supply or artwork?
Any 'yes' means the change has its own timeline.
Treat each pre-launch change as a mini-project; late changes cause late surprises.

exercises.scenario: Purchasing moves lactose to a new supplier, same grade.

options: QA, and possibly RA; artwork unaffected
Artwork and marketing, since lactose is declared on the pack

questions.prompt: Which change most likely needs stability, a variation and supply planning?
options: A new font on the carton

exercises.scenario: Three weeks before launch, someone proposes 'just a small change next week'.

options: Approve it, since small changes are fine
Run the four questions first: QA, RA, stability, supply or artwork
Ask the QP to sign it off

questions.prompt: What's the most common source of late surprises?

summary.title: What's in the pack
points: Tablets, primary pack, leaflet, carton and safety features each have supplier, spec and lead time.
Excipients with known effect must be declared, linking formulation to artwork.
Primary packaging is quality data: changes need stability and a variation.
The carton carries the legal particulars, Braille, Blue Box and safety features.
Printed items follow artwork approval and come last.

exercises.scenario: A partner proposes a cheaper film and a lactose-based filler, six months before launch.

options: The filler only, since excipients drive stability more than packaging
Only if the film is coloured

questions.prompt: Explain why printed components often arrive last.
questions.modelAnswer: Blister foil, leaflets and cartons can only be printed after the country artwork is approved, and then the printer needs its lead time, so they come at the end of the chain.

exercises.scenario: Your carton is missing the pack size and the excipient declaration.

questions.prompt: What's the status of the artwork?
options: Fine: pack size appears on the blister
Fine: excipients are declared only in the leaflet
Not compliant: both are required particulars

summary.title: Suppliers, devices and change
points: Only GMP-approved suppliers may deliver; qualification depth follows risk.
A new launch supplier must be approved before printing or delivery.
Separate devices need CE marking; integral ones need a notified-body opinion.
Four questions for any change: QA, RA, stability, supply or artwork.
Any 'yes' turns a change into a mini-project.

exercises.scenario: To catch a launch date, purchasing wants a new, unapproved leaflet printer.

options: QA qualification of the printer and change control
A Type II variation and a new readability test of the leaflet

questions.prompt: Which of the four questions is most likely 'yes' here?
options: QA: supplier qualification and change control

questions.prompt: List the four questions to ask about any proposed change.
questions.modelAnswer: Does QA need change control or supplier qualification? Does RA need a variation, and of which type? Does it affect stability? Does it touch supply or artwork?

exercises.scenario: A product line adds an oral syringe as a separate device.

options: Supplier qualification, CE marking and the syringe's lead time
A notified-body opinion in the application
questions.explanation: A separate device is CE-marked on its own.

options: RA, because supplier changes need variations

summary.title: The finished product: the whole picture
points: A pack is tablets, primary pack, leaflet, carton and safety features, each with its own lead time.
Excipients with known effect link formulation to artwork.
Primary packaging is quality data; changes need stability and a variation.
The carton carries the legal particulars and must fit a fixed format.
Only qualified suppliers may deliver; devices need CE marking or a notified-body opinion.
Run the four change questions; late changes are the main source of surprises.

exercises.scenario: You build a component list for a three-country tablet launch.

options: Only the price per unit from the latest quote
questions.explanation: Any one can hold up a launch.

questions.prompt: Which component change is most disruptive?

options: As soon as each country's artwork is final
questions.explanation: Then the printer's lead time starts.

exercises.scenario: Four weeks before launch, two changes appear: a new carton printer and a new film supplier for the same film.

questions.prompt: Which can more likely be absorbed?
options: The film supplier, since the film is the same material
The printer, if QA qualifies it in time
questions.explanation: Primary packaging changes reach stability and possibly RA.

questions.prompt: What do you do with each?
options: Run the four questions and give each an owner and dates
Wait until after launch to look
Approve both now and check the effects after launch

questions.prompt: Explain in two sentences why one component change rarely stays local.
questions.modelAnswer: Each component is tied to a specification, a supplier, the dossier and often the artwork. So a change can need supplier qualification, a variation, stability data and new printed material, each with its own timeline.
